# PRD: Self-Service Password Reset

## Functional Requirements

### FR-001: Self-Service Password Reset via Email Link
**Statement:** As a registered user, I want to reset my own password via a time-limited emailed link, so that I can regain account access without contacting support.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**
| Category | Boundary Condition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Performance | Reset email must be delivered within 60 seconds of request | Stakeholder interview, Security team |
| Security | Reset link must expire after 15 minutes and be single-use | Security team standard |

### FR-002: Account Lockout After Failed Reset Attempts
**Statement:** As a system, the reset flow must lock an account after repeated failed attempts, so that reset links cannot be brute-forced.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**
| Category | Boundary Condition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Security | Lockout after 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes | Security team standard |

### FR-003: Password Complexity Validation
**Statement:** As a user, when setting a new password, I want it validated against complexity rules, so that weak passwords are rejected.

**Non-Functional Requirements:**
| Category | Boundary Condition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Compliance | New passwords must meet NIST 800-63B guidelines | Compliance team |

## Assumptions
- **Verified email on file** (underlies FR-001): We assume all active users have a verified email address on file; unverified accounts are out of scope for self-service reset.

## Constraints
- **Reuse existing Auth Service token infrastructure** (constrains FR-001, FR-002): No new IAM system may be introduced; reset tokens must be issued by the existing Auth Service.

## Risks
- **Shared lockout module regression** (affects FR-002, program-level): Modifying the shared lockout module could affect the standard login flow, not just password reset.

## Open Questions
- FR-003 (Compliance): TBD whether the NIST 800-63B complexity rule applies retroactively to existing passwords, or only to newly set ones.
impact_assessment:
# Impact Assessment: Self-Service Password Reset

## Impact Summary
Overall Impact Level: Medium

## Existing-System Impact
| Existing System (CI) | Touched? | How / Why Not | Component(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auth Service | Yes | Adds reset-token issuance path and a lockout module change | FR-001, FR-002 |
| Notification Service | Yes | Sends the password-reset email | FR-001 |
| CRM | No | Password reset does not touch customer profile data | — |
| Billing Service | No | Unrelated to authentication | — |

## Components Identified
| Requirement | Component (new/existing) | Blast Radius | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | Password Reset API (new) | Medium | New endpoint, but reuses existing Auth Service token infrastructure |
| FR-001 | Email Template Service (existing) | Low | Minor addition of a new email template |
| FR-002 | Auth Service Lockout Module (existing) | High | Shared module change affects all login flows, not just reset |
| FR-003 | Password Validation Library (existing) | Low | Shared validation utility gets a new ruleset |

## External Dependencies
- Email delivery depends on the existing third-party provider, SendGrid; no new procurement needed.

## Flags & Data Quality
None — CMDB records for Auth Service and Notification Service were current as of assessment date.
